name: MonarchColumnChooser
title: ColumnChooser
wrapsNative: List with a Section, Toggle per column and ForEach.onMove(perform:); accessibilityActions for Move up and Move down; a TextField search row
summary: A panel to show, hide, find and reorder the columns of a table, for a sheet, a settings screen or a saved-view editor.
whenToUse: To let people choose which columns a MonarchDataTable shows and in what order, usually in a sheet opened from a Columns button.
whenNotToUse: For a short list of on/off settings, use Toggles in a Form. For reordering other things, use a List with onMove (reorderable-list).
api: init(_ columns: [MonarchColumnChooserColumn], hiddenColumns: Binding<Set<String>>, order: Binding<[String]>? = nil, searchThreshold: Int = 8, minimumVisible: Int = 1, labels: MonarchColumnChooserLabels = MonarchColumnChooserLabels(), onReset: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil)
MonarchColumnChooserColumn.init(_ label: String, id: String? = nil, isHideable: Bool = true)

struct MonarchColumnChooserLabels { var title, search, noMatches, required, showAll, reset: String?; var shownCount: (@Sendable (Int, Int) -> String)?; var moveUp, moveDown: (@Sendable (String) -> String)?; var moved: (@Sendable (String, Int, Int) -> String)? }

options.name: columns
options.description: The columns in their default order. MonarchDataTableColumn.chooserColumn gives one.

options.name: hiddenColumns
options.description: The ids of hidden columns, the same set MonarchDataTable takes.

options.name: order
options.description: Column ids in display order. With it, rows reorder with onMove and accessibility actions; ids missing from it follow in their default order.

options.name: searchThreshold
options.description: Offers the search field from this many columns. Pass Int.max for never.

options.name: minimumVisible
options.description: The fewest columns that must stay shown; the last ones cannot be switched off.

options.name: onReset
options.description: Adds a Reset button that runs this, to restore the app's default columns.

states.name: default
states.description: A switch per column, on when it is shown, with "5 of 8 shown" under the title.

states.name: required column
states.description: Always on and disabled, with "Always shown" under its name.

states.name: minimum reached
states.description: The switches of the last shown columns are disabled.

states.name: searching
states.description: Only matching columns are listed, reordering is off, and "No columns match." is shown when nothing matches.

states.name: some hidden
states.description: A Show all button appears under the list.

appearance: A system list. The title is subheading text in the default role and the count caption text in the muted role; notes, the search icon and the no-match text use the muted role. Switches are the system's and take the theme's accent tint. Show all and Reset are small ghost MonarchButtons. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes come from these roles.
platformNotes: The web panel moves columns with Move up and Move down icon buttons; on iOS rows reorder with List.onMove (drag a row, or the reorder controls when the app puts the list in edit mode), and VoiceOver users get Move up and Move down as accessibility actions. The web uses checkboxes; iOS uses the platform switch. The web takes a visibility record; on iOS it is the set of hidden ids. The search is a field inside the list rather than .searchable, so it works without a navigation container. The web headingLevel has no equivalent; the title has the header trait. Android uses the same name and options.
accessibility: The title and count are one header element: "Columns, 5 of 8 shown".
Each column is a standard switch read with its name, its note and its state.
Columns that cannot be hidden and the last shown columns are disabled switches.
With order, each row has the accessibility actions "Move Status up" and "Move Status down" (only where the move is possible), and every move is announced.
The clear-search button is named "Clear search" and has a 44-point touch target.
edgeCases: Ids in order that no longer exist are skipped; new columns follow in their default order.
Search ignores case and diacritics and trims spaces.
Show all also clears hidden ids of columns that are not listed.
The panel is a List and fills its space; present it in a sheet or give it a frame.

examples.title: Next to a DataTable
examples.template:
VStack(spacing: 16) {
    MonarchColumnChooser(
        columns.map(\.chooserColumn),
        hiddenColumns: $hidden,
        order: $order,
        onReset: { hidden = [{{hidden.0}}]; order = [] }
    )
    .frame(height: 440)
    MonarchDataTable(
        {{caption}},
        rows: records,
        columns: columns,
        hiddenColumns: hidden,
        columnOrder: order
    )
    .frame(height: 300)
}
examples.setupTemplate:
struct Record: Identifiable, Sendable {
    let id: String
    let name: String
    let status: String
    let owner: String
    let region: String
    let renews: String
}

private let records = [
    Record(id: {{rows.0.id}}, name: {{rows.0.name}}, status: {{rows.0.status}}, owner: {{rows.0.owner}}, region: {{rows.0.region}}, renews: {{rows.0.renews}}),
    Record(id: {{rows.1.id}}, name: {{rows.1.name}}, status: {{rows.1.status}}, owner: {{rows.1.owner}}, region: {{rows.1.region}}, renews: {{rows.1.renews}}),
    Record(id: {{rows.2.id}}, name: {{rows.2.name}}, status: {{rows.2.status}}, owner: {{rows.2.owner}}, region: {{rows.2.region}}, renews: {{rows.2.renews}}),
]
private let columns: [MonarchDataTableColumn<Record>] = [
    MonarchDataTableColumn({{columns.0.header}}, id: {{columns.0.id}}, isHideable: {{columns.0.hideable}}, value: { $0.name }),
    MonarchDataTableColumn({{columns.1.header}}, id: {{columns.1.id}}, value: { $0.status }),
    MonarchDataTableColumn({{columns.2.header}}, id: {{columns.2.id}}, value: { $0.owner }),
    MonarchDataTableColumn({{columns.3.header}}, id: {{columns.3.id}}, value: { $0.region }),
    MonarchDataTableColumn({{columns.4.header}}, id: {{columns.4.id}}, value: { $0.renews }),
]
@State private var hidden: Set<String> = [{{hidden.0}}]
@State private var order: [String] = []
examples.setup:
struct Record: Identifiable, Sendable {
    let id: String
    let name: String
    let status: String
    let owner: String
    let region: String
    let renews: String
}

private let records = [
    Record(id: "1", name: "Alpha", status: "Active", owner: "Sam Lee", region: "EU", renews: "2027-02-01"),
    Record(id: "2", name: "Bravo", status: "Paused", owner: "Ana Ruiz", region: "US", renews: "2026-11-30"),
    Record(id: "3", name: "Charlie", status: "Active", owner: "Kim Park", region: "APAC", renews: "2027-06-15"),
]
private let columns: [MonarchDataTableColumn<Record>] = [
    MonarchDataTableColumn("Name", id: "name", isHideable: false, value: { $0.name }),
    MonarchDataTableColumn("Status", id: "status", value: { $0.status }),
    MonarchDataTableColumn("Owner", id: "owner", value: { $0.owner }),
    MonarchDataTableColumn("Region", id: "region", value: { $0.region }),
    MonarchDataTableColumn("Renews", id: "renews", value: { $0.renews }),
]
@State private var hidden: Set<String> = ["region"]
@State private var order: [String] = []
examples.code:
VStack(spacing: 16) {
    MonarchColumnChooser(
        columns.map(\.chooserColumn),
        hiddenColumns: $hidden,
        order: $order,
        onReset: { hidden = ["region"]; order = [] }
    )
    .frame(height: 440)
    MonarchDataTable(
        "Records",
        rows: records,
        columns: columns,
        hiddenColumns: hidden,
        columnOrder: order
    )
    .frame(height: 300)
}
